record.paper_title: Noncommutative spectral geometry of Riemannian foliations: some results and open problems
record.original_question: Let F be an arbitrary foliation on a compact Riemannian manifold. If D_F = d_F + d_F^* is the leafwise signature operator on M, D_{F_N} is the corresponding leafwise signature operator on the conormal bundle N^*F relative to the linearized foliation F_N, D_H = d_H + d_H^* is the transverse signature operator on M, and sigma(D_H) is its transverse principal symbol acting by multiplication on N^*F, does the asymptotic formula tr f(D_F + h D_H) = (2 pi)^{-q} h^{-q} tr_{F_N} f(D_{F_N} + sigma(D_H)) + o(h^{-q}) hold as h -> 0 for every even compactly supported smooth function f?

evidence.quote: To extend the above conjecture to the Laplace operator on M, we can try to use the corresponding signature operators.

Conjecture 3.16. Let F be an arbitrary foliation on a compact Riemannian manifold. For any even function f in C_c^infinity(R), the asymptotic formula holds: tr f(D_F + hD_H) = (2pi)^{-q} h^{-q} tr_{F_N} f(D_{F_N} + sigma(D_H)) + o(h^{-q}), h -> 0.

where D_F = d_F + d_F^* is the leafwise signature operator on M, D_{F_N} is the corresponding leafwise (relative to F_N) signature operator on N^*F, D_H = d_H + d_H^* is the transverse signature operator on M, sigma(D_H) is the transverse principal symbol of D_H.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold equipped with a smooth foliation $F$ of codimension $q$. Let $T F\subset T M$ denote the tangent bundle of $F$ and let $H = (T F)^{\perp}\subset T M$ be the orthogonal complement, identified with the normal bundle $N F$; let $N^{*} F$ denote the conormal bundle. Decompose the de Rham differential as $d = d_F + d_H + \theta$, where $d_F$ is the leafwise (tangential) component and $d_H$ is the transverse component. Define the leafwise signature operator $D_F = d_F + d_F^{*}$ acting on $\Omega^{\bullet}(M)$, and the transverse signature operator $D_H = d_H + d_H^{*}$. Let $\sigma(D_H)$ denote the transverse principal symbol of $D_H$, viewed as a bundle endomorphism acting by Clifford-type multiplication by elements of $N^{*} F$. Let $F_N$ denote the linearized foliation on the total space of $N^{*} F$ obtained by lifting the leaves of $F$ via the linearized holonomy, and let $D_{F_N} = d_{F_N} + d_{F_N}^{*}$ be the corresponding leafwise signature operator on $N^{*} F$ relative to $F_N$. Let $\operatorname{tr}_{F_N}$ denote the transverse (Connes) trace associated with $F_N$.

For each $h>0$ consider the perturbed operator $D_F + h D_H$ on $M$. Prove or disprove: for every even function $f \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$, the asymptotic formula
$$\operatorname{tr} f(D_F + h D_H) = (2\pi)^{-q} h^{-q} \operatorname{tr}_{F_N} f(D_{F_N} + \sigma(D_H)) + o(h^{-q})$$
holds as $h \to 0^{+}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture in the survey on noncommutative spectral geometry of Riemannian foliations by Kordyukov, who indicates it as an attempted extension to signature operators of an earlier semiclassical-asymptotics conjecture for leafwise Laplacians. No subsequent paper resolving the conjecture was located via web search; related work by Kordyukov and collaborators on adiabatic limits and semiclassical asymptotics for leafwise Laplacians proves results in adjacent settings but does not establish this signature-operator asymptotic. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Adiabatic Limits and the Spectrum of the Laplacian on Foliated Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral asymptotics of the Laplacian under adiabatic blow-up on Riemannian foliations.
status_evidence.claim: Related adiabatic-limit results exist for the leafwise Laplacian, but no resolution of the signature-operator version is reported.

status_evidence.title: Adiabatic limits and spectral sequences for Riemannian foliations
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral asymptotics under adiabatic limit on Riemannian foliations are described via the differentiable spectral sequence.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent work on adiabatic asymptotics; no proof of the conjectured signature-operator formula was found.
